title: Decide whether lore scaffold docusaurus should pin its unpinned scaffold-time dependency resolution
description: The docusaurus scaffold's algolia search-integration dependencies are resolved unpinned at scaffold time (npm install against whatever docusaurus's own published template currently references). On 2026-09-09 that transitive resolution broke CI twice in an afternoon -- two different algolia sub-packages, both at 5.59.0, both failing to resolve from the registry -- confirmed as an upstream registry issue, not a lore-cli defect, and confirmed RESOLVED the same day (see notes). The acute outage is over; what remains open is whether lore should pin/vendor a known-good algolia dependency set in the scaffolded docusaurus template to prevent a recurrence, or accept that an unpinned transitive dependency can take this smoke test down again with no guarantee of how long it takes upstream to recover next time.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Decide: pin/vendor a known-good algolia search dependency set in the docusaurus scaffold template, or explicitly accept the unpinned-transitive-dependency risk as acceptable for a smoke test (not a released artifact)
If pinning is chosen, implement it and verify the scaffold smoke test still passes against the pinned versions
If accepting the risk is chosen, record that decision here so a future recurrence is recognized as an accepted, known risk rather than investigated fresh

implementationNotes:
OUTAGE CONFIRMED RESOLVED (2026-09-09, dated so this doesn't sit stale). This task originally described the acute failure directly; narrowed above once the outage itself resolved, per opum-agent: an open task describing a condition that no longer exists is the same stale-record class as everything else cleared today.

Confirmation, not just relief: the diagnosis (external, upstream, unrelated to lore-cli's own changes) was made BEFORE the resolution, on plausibility -- nothing in the CLAUDE.md-prose-plus-ci.yml-comment PR that first hit this could touch docusaurus scaffolding. PR #636's promotion run (a later, unrelated SHA) ran the full matrix clean, including docusaurus scaffold smoke passing outright -- confirming the prediction rather than merely ending the problem. That is the evidence this note exists to record: run https://github.com/opum-ai/lore-cli/actions/runs/34372155086, job 'docusaurus scaffold smoke', pass, 1m26s.

What's still open, and why this stays a task rather than closing: the underlying exposure (unpinned transitive algolia dependency, resolved fresh at scaffold time) is unchanged. Nothing prevents a recurrence; today's incident just happened to self-resolve within the hour. That's the pinning decision the narrowed title/ACs above now ask for.

Re-titled and ranked low per opum-doc ruling ODOC-480: the real question is the unpinned scaffold-time resolution (algolia packages were the 2026-09-09 instance); no algolia pin exists in the repo to guard.

Kept as the surviving record of the LCLI-463/470 pair per ODOC-480 grooming ruling 2026-11-04 (opum-ai/opum-doc#1621): LCLI-470 (restore the widened scope) is closed as superseded by this record. The widened scope is NOT applied here: it would retitle this to which of the repo CI-time external dependency fetches are worth pinning or caching, on the reasoning that two npm/algolia resolution failures and one Chrome apt Hash Sum mismatch in one day are one exposure class. That widened copy stays archived at /Volumes/external/archive/lore-cli/pre-purge-unlanded-work/LCLI-463-widened.json with its NOTE.md. Whether to widen is the owner decision this task already asks for.
